subject: Re: Follow-up & DPA clarifications for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev.patel@acmepayments.com>; Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmepayments.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Hi Sanjeev / Laura —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Key needs: PII handling, configurable data retention, detailed request/response logging for audits, and options for data residency in us-east-1.
- Integration: You plan to send payment metadata and tokenized PII to Redwood for inference; raw card data will not be sent to our API.
- Compliance asks: DPA clarifications around controller vs processor roles, subprocessors list and notification window for breaches, and options for deleting customer data on request.

Action items we agreed: 
1) I will share our standard DPA and a short Q&A addressing controller/processor roles and subprocessors. (attached)
2) David will follow up with details about logging controls and retention configuration.
3) Laura to confirm timeline for legal review and whether Acme needs a redline.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (our standard), acme_privacy_questions.docx (notes from call).

If helpful, we can set a short call with our Legal/Privacy partner (Rachel) — is Thursday morning PT open?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev.patel@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmepayments.com>, Tim O'Rourke <tim.orourke@acmepayments.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T17:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few clarifying questions after a quick review: 

1) Controller vs Processor: Our legal team views Acme as the controller and Redwood as a processor. We need explicit language that confirms Redwood will only process data per our documented instructions and won't use Acme data for model training or product improvement without consent. Can you confirm?

2) Subprocessors: Please provide the current subprocessors list and confirm the notification window if Redwood adds a new subprocessor. We typically ask for 30 days' notice and the opportunity to object.

3) Breach notification: We need a committed timeline for breach notification (we prefer 72 hours). The DPA mentions "without undue delay" — can Redwood commit to a tighter SLA?

4) Data deletion & retention: For logs and request/response artifacts, can we configure retention down to 30 days, and do you support on-demand deletion for specific customer datasets?

If possible, could you have someone from Privacy/Legal respond to the above in writing? Laura is tracking timelines on our side.

— Sanjeev
Sanjeev Patel
Head of Privacy, Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev.patel@acmepayments.com>; Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmepayments.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-19T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Hi Sanjeev — thanks for the detailed questions. Looping in Rachel (Legal) and David (Solutions) to provide written answers. Quick responses below while they weigh in: 

1) Training use: Redwood does not use customer input data to retrain public models unless there is explicit, opt-in agreement in the contract. We'll ensure the DPA includes a sentence to that effect.

2) Subprocessors: I'll attach the current subprocessors list. Our standard practice is 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; we'll confirm that in writing.

3) Breach notice: Rachel — can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 72-hour initial notification window? If not, what's the proposed SLA?

4) Retention & deletion: David — can you confirm support for 30-day retention and on-demand deletion APIs for customer datasets/keys?

Thanks — we'll follow up with a redline or confirmation by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev.patel@acmepayments.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-19T13:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Hi Sanjeev / Laura —

Thanks for flagging these items. Written responses below for your legal team's review: 

- Controller/Processor: We confirm Redwood will act as a processor and process data only on documented instructions. We will add explicit non-use language to the DPA: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve models or services without Customer's prior written consent."

- Subprocessors: Our current subprocessors (as of 2026-02-19) are listed in the attached PDF. Redwood will provide at least 30 calendar days' notice prior to engaging any new subprocessor and will allow Customer to object in writing. If Acme objects, Redwood will work in good faith to offer alternatives, including termination rights for that subprocessor if no remedy is available.

- Breach notification: Redwood's standard DPA uses "without undue delay" language. We can commit to an initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware of a qualifying security incident, followed by regular updates as we investigate. We will include that 72-hour initial notification SLA in the redlined DPA.

- Data retention & deletion: Redwood supports configurable retention policies at the customer level; the platform can be configured to retain logs and request/response artifacts for as little as 30 days. We also provide an on-demand deletion API and can coordinate a one-time purge for historical data related to a contract. Operational steps and timelines are outlined in the attached note from our SRE team.

Please review the attached Redlines (see DocuSign link) and let us know any further items you want us to address. Happy to join a follow-up call if that helps accelerate review.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmepayments.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev.patel@acmepayments.com>, Tim O'Rourke <tim.orourke@acmepayments.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. Laura from Acme Legal here. A few follow-ups: 

- Appreciate the 72-hour commit. We will circulate the redline internally.
- We expect to provide a consolidated redline by Friday. At that point, can we schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call to run through items that remain in dispute? Thursday is tight for us, so Friday afternoon PT works.

We also noticed the subprocessors PDF references a logging provider (LogStream Inc.) — can you confirm whether LogStream receives pseudonymized request IDs only, or any PII elements? If LogStream receives any PII, we will flag it in our review.

I'll confirm the redline timeline by EOD. Thanks again for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Laura Chen
Senior Counsel, Acme Payments
laura.chen@acmepayments.com
